Welcome to Kelvin Grove School
Welcome to Kelvin Grove. We are a three-form entry primary school situated in Upper Sydenham in the London Borough of Lewisham. We have a 24 place Resource Base provision for pupils with a diagnosis of Autism or similar social communication need. There is a nursery provision offering both full time and part time places (15/30 hours). We have a well-established on-site breakfast and afterschool provision which supports families with childcare needs 7.45am – 6.00pm. We have built a thriving, inclusive school community where all children are proud of their achievements and excel in their learning.
Our curriculum is designed to develop in all, a lifelong love of learning and all children are taught the knowledge, skills and values they need to be successful and contribute positively to the diverse world in which they live. Our partnership with home allows us to inform and maintain our high standards of learning and behaviour.
If you are a prospective parent for our reception class intake, please book a tour of the school using the booking form below. If you are looking for a place for your child in Year 1 to Year 6 or our resource base, please contact the school.
Tours take place with Ian Hyde on Tuesdays at 9.45am for prospective Reception class parents. BOOK HERE
If you are not a prospective Reception class parent, please contact the school and we would be happy to arrange a suitable time for you to visit.

Phonics and Early Reading Policy
Reviewed by: Eben Groenewald, Achievement Committee, Spring 2025
Next Review: Spring 2026
Kelvin Grove is a three-form entry primary school with an ASD Resource Base and a nursery. There are currently 540 pupils on roll.
Roughly 30% of the children in each year have FSM and qualify for the Pupil Premium. 41% of pupils have English as an additional language. We have children from 15 different ethnic groups, with the largest groups being White British, Black British African and Black British Caribbean. The school has about 21% of pupils who receive SEND provision and 10% of our SEND pupils have an EHCP. The school’s stability is slightly lower than the national average.
Our rate of fixed term exclusions is also lower than the national average, with no permanent exclusions in the past three years. We have a slightly higher rate of absence than the national average, as well as a higher rate of persistent absenteeism.
Inclusion is at the heart of everything we do. Visitors to the school comment on the friendly, warm welcome they receive from the children and the positive learning environment. The curriculum is designed to develop a love of learning and an embedding of skills and knowledge. It is essential that our approach to teaching phonics and reading is accessible to all learners, regardless of background.
Phonics (reading and spelling)
At Kelvin Grove, we believe that all our children can become fluent readers and writers. This is why we teach reading through Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised, which is a systematic and synthetic phonics programme. We start teaching phonics in Nursery/Reception and follow the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised progression, which ensures children build on their growing knowledge of the alphabetic code, mastering phonics to read and spell as they move through school.
As a result, all our children are able to tackle any unfamiliar words as they read. At Kelvin Grove, we also model the application of the alphabetic code through phonics in shared reading and writing, both inside and outside of the phonics lesson and across the curriculum. We have a strong focus on language development for our children because we know that speaking and listening are crucial skills for reading and writing in all subjects.
At Kelvin Grove, we value reading as a crucial life skill. By the time children leave us, they read confidently for meaning and regularly enjoy reading for pleasure. Our readers are equipped with the tools to tackle unfamiliar vocabulary. We encourage our children to see themselves as readers for both pleasure and purpose.
Because we believe teaching every child to read is so important, we have a Reading Leader who drives the early reading programme in our school. This person is highly skilled at teaching phonics and reading, and they monitor and support our reading team, so everyone teaches with fidelity to the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised programme.

Ensuring reading for pleasure
‘Reading for pleasure is the single most important indicator of a child’s success.’ (OECD 2002)
‘The will influences the skill and vice versa.’ (OECD 2010)
We value reading for pleasure highly and work hard as a school to grow our Reading for Pleasure pedagogy.
Assessment is used to monitor progress and to identify any child needing additional support as soon as they need it.

Welcome from the Chair of Governors
Kelvin Grove is a diverse and inclusive school, fully representative of our local community. We are able to welcome pupils of all abilities and serve a wide range of needs, meaning we are immensely proud of the progress all of our pupils make throughout their time here – not just academically, but socially and emotionally. In our most recent inspection OFSTED recognised the strong community we have and the support and care this provides for everyone.
We want to ensure that we stay true to our vision of every child developing a lifelong love of learning. This means a strong focus on the core curriculum areas of reading, writing and maths, coupled with a forward thinking and progressive wider curriculum – ensuring that every child can thrive. Our music provision sets us apart, with a range of music lessons and clubs accessible to all. A wide array of extra-curricular activities and school residential trips, in the UK and France, ensure that life at Kelvin Grove is stimulating and memorable.

We help set the direction for the school and work closely with the Leadership Team on a supportive and, where necessary, challenging basis. We hold decision makers to account and bring healthy, alternative perspectives to the team.

I’m proud to be both a parent and a Governor at KG and to have the opportunity to give something back to the school that has given my children, and others, so much.
Please do contact me if you have any questions.

Governors’ Code of Conduct
Reviewed by: Full Governing Body Meeting Thursday 28th September 2023
Next Review: Full Governing Body, Autumn 2024
We agree to abide by the Seven Nolan Principles of Public Life:
We will act solely in terms of the public interest.
We will avoid placing ourselves under any obligation to people or organisations that might try inappropriately to influence us in our work. We will not act or take decisions in order to gain financial or other material benefits for ourselves, our family, or our friends. We will declare and resolve any interests and relationships.
We will act and take decisions impartially, fairly and on merit, using the best evidence and without discrimination or bias.
We are accountable to the public for our decisions and actions and will submit ourselves to the scrutiny necessary to ensure this.
We will act and take decisions in an open and transparent manner. Information will not be withheld from the public unless there are clear and lawful reasons for so doing.
We will be truthful.
We will exhibit these principles in our own behaviour. We will actively promote and robustly support the principles and be willing to challenge poor behaviour wherever it occurs.

We understand that potential or perceived breaches of this code will be taken seriously and that a breach could lead to formal sanctions.

Curriculum Intent @KG
At Kelvin Grove we aim to provide a curriculum which ignites curiosity in our children and will enable them to become motivated, resilient and successful learners.
At the heart of our curriculum is the well-being of our pupils. We are working hard to ensure effective practice and provision is in place that promotes emotional well-being, embedding an ethos where mental health is regarded as the responsibility of all.
Staff at Kelvin Grove work collaboratively to build upon the requirements of the National Curriculum through ambitious, enquiry-led learning opportunities. We design Learning Journeys with clear subject specialisms, making meaningful links between them. These enable children to develop skills in different subject areas, acquiring a depth of knowledge which they build upon year after year. Learning Journeys provide opportunities for pupils to apply English and maths across the wider curriculum. We create memorable experiences for our pupils through topic launches, visits and visitors – using the wealth of local resources to good advantage.
We aim for pupils to develop a rich and subject-specific vocabulary and nurturing a love of reading across the curriculum is key to this. All staff have high expectations of pupil talk and understand that classroom dialogue is essential to thinking and learning.
All school leaders play a vital role in designing the curriculum, ensuring that it reflects the community we serve. Through regular monitoring and evaluation, we review the teaching and learning of different subjects.
All curriculum leaders play a vital role in curriculum design, and through regular monitoring and evaluation, they review the teaching and learning of different subjects.
Kelvin Grove provides a highly inclusive environment where all learners at all levels are helped to achieve. The curriculum design ensures that the needs of individual and small groups of children can be met within the environment of high quality teaching, supported by targeted, high quality interventions where appropriate. Our school endeavours to grow and maintain strong community links which give our pupils a true sense of belonging.
